newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: U.S. says NATO no threat to Russia.
newsitem.headline: U.S. says NATO no threat to Russia.

text.p: The United States told a European security summit on Monday that NATO expansion posed no threat to Russia or any other country and that the alliance's planned enlargement would help bring stability to the whole continent.
"NATO has been and remains a defensive alliance...it poses no threat to any other state," Vice President Al Gore told leaders from more than 50 nations at the summit in Lisbon.

Gore was speaking just after Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin renewed Moscow's attack on NATO plans to admit countries from Central and Eastern Europe, which will probably include former Soviet satellites like Poland and Hungary.
"The stability that NATO can help extend to Central Europe can help ensure the security of all nations," said Gore.
Gore said the United States and NATO wanted to develop a strong cooperative relationship with Russia as well.
Washington, he said, remained committed "to building a new Europe undivided and at peace".
